actual_prs.title: Support empty higher-dimensional Euclidean pairwise sets
actual_prs.head: be246bc9b2e9ac3b155a117ded22811a02534135
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

`Euclidean(ndim > 1).pairwise_inner` and `cdist` flatten manifold axes with an inferred `-1` reshape. Empty point sets or an empty leading batch axis make that dimension ambiguous and raise instead of returning the correctly shaped empty pairwise result. Filtering away all matrix-valued or tensor-valued points therefore breaks these public operations.

Flatten only the trailing manifold axes explicitly. This preserves the point and broadcast batch axes, supports noncontiguous inputs, and keeps the existing calculations for nonempty inputs.

## Validation

- Unchanged upstream: **40 failures, 8 passing controls**.
- Both operations, float32/float64, two- and three-dimensional manifolds, empty left/right/both sets, broadcast empty sets, empty batch axes, and ordinary nonempty controls.
- Independent references broadcast the original manifold-shaped points and reduce products or vector norms. Output shapes, dtype, values, and gradients are checked with noncontiguous input views.
- New regressions plus existing Euclidean and manifold-basic suites: **2,159 passed, 310 skipped** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff passes.
- [Reproducible original/candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43849373630).

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43849974864/job/133239701648) stops in `Setup Python 3.8`, before dependency installation or tests: Python 3.8 is unavailable on its Ubuntu 26.04 runner. The [unchanged base job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43672079266/job/132684116427) fails for the same reason; the runner pin is already proposed in #300.

The separate validation above uses Ubuntu 24.04 and checks this exact head on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0: **2,159 passed, 310 skipped** per environment. These passing results do not change the failed upstream check status.

actual_prs.title: Use a linear-time queue for synthetic tree generation
actual_prs.head: 169899d014727842cceee661f3ba89e72ad78290
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

The breadth-first tree generator removes each pending node with `list.pop(0)`. Every removal shifts the remaining entries, so wide trees spend quadratic work maintaining the traversal queue.

Use `collections.deque` and `popleft()` while preserving the existing FIFO traversal and random draw order.

## Validation and measured effect

- The existing dataset suite passes before and after the change: **32 passed** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff passes.
- An end-to-end benchmark constructs real `StereographicTreeDataset` instances, including geometric sampling and sibling generation. Every output tensor, three indexed samples, the class count, and the final PyTorch RNG state have identical SHA-256 digests before and after the change.
- CPU, one thread, Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0; medians of three runs with the same seed, dimension 2 and one sibling per node:

| Tree | Original | deque | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Binary, depth 8, 511 nodes | 0.1046 s | 0.1037 s | 1.01x |
| 100,000 children, depth 1, 100,001 nodes | 13.2191 s | 12.0607 s | 1.10x |
| 300,000 children, depth 1, 300,001 nodes | 43.6490 s | 36.5074 s | 1.20x |

The gain grows with queue width; small-tree generation is effectively unchanged in this measurement. These are complete CPU dataset-construction timings, not GPU or training-loop results.

[Reproducible original/candidate tests, benchmark, and output-equivalence checks](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43848030563).

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43849787064/job/133239057637) stops in `Setup Python 3.8`, before dependency installation or tests: Python 3.8 is unavailable on its Ubuntu 26.04 runner. The [unchanged base job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43672079266/job/132684116427) fails for the same reason; the runner pin is already proposed in #300.

The separate validation above uses Ubuntu 24.04 and checks this exact head on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0: **32 passed** per environment. These passing results do not change the failed upstream check status.

actual_prs.title: Keep synthetic tree tensors on the manifold dtype and device
actual_prs.head: b5728f97ff3834d3ba0ad7d048df4310cb39668b
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

`StereographicTreeDataset` creates its root, random directions, and step scalar with global tensor defaults. A float64 manifold therefore receives float32 tree geometry under the usual defaults, and the reverse mismatch also occurs. CUDA manifolds additionally receive CPU intermediates.

Create the root with the manifold dtype/device, and create directions and the distance scalar from the parent tensor. This retains the requested geometry precision throughout tree construction.

## Validation

- Unchanged upstream: **16 failures, 16 passing controls**, with 2 CUDA checks skipped.

- New regressions and the existing dataset suite: **64 passed, 2 skipped** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff passes.
- CUDA checks are included but were not executed on the CPU runners.
- [Reproducible original/candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43847783215).

actual_prs.title: Respect curvature in Lorentz polar projection
actual_prs.head: a790cf689ab6493917b5622d96c4dee93b007f93
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

`lorentz.math.project_polar` scales the spatial coordinates by `sqrt(k)` but leaves the time coordinate unscaled. For `k != 1`, even zero radius maps to the wrong hyperboloid origin, and general polar points violate the defining Minkowski constraint. The derivative with respect to a learnable curvature is incorrect even when evaluated at `k = 1`.

Apply the same curvature scale to the time coordinate, and correct the documented time-first coordinate formula and polar input description.

## Validation

- Unchanged upstream: **24 failures, 6 passing controls**.
- Float32/float64, four curvature values, three coordinate-axis positions, batched directions, and zero/positive/negative radii.
- Checks the Minkowski constraint, exact zero-radius origin, radial distance, and agreement with the independent exponential-map construction.
- Radius and curvature gradients match that exponential-map construction, including the unit-curvature case.
- New regressions plus existing Lorentz math, coordinates, transport, manifold-axis, and neural-layer suites: **447 passed** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff passes.
- [Reproducible original/candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43846195005).

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43846977619/job/133229489919) stops in `Setup Python 3.8`, before dependency installation or tests: Python 3.8 is unavailable on its Ubuntu 26.04 runner. actual_prs.title: Avoid unnecessary eigenvectors in SPD membership checks
actual_prs.head: 8412752c9805672cc691a003ed97c21ff6ee1bf3
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

SPD membership validation computes a full eigenbasis and then discards it. For tensors that require gradients, it also builds differentiable spectral state even though the public result is only a boolean and optional explanation.

Use eigenvalues only on a detached view. Symmetry checks, upper-triangle selection, the existing eigenvalue tolerance, and caller-owned tensor/gradient state remain unchanged.

## Validation

- The same 16 behavior checks pass before and after the change: positive/repeated/zero/near-threshold/negative spectra, batched rejection, symmetry explanations, noncontiguous inputs, and preservation of caller gradients.
- New checks plus existing SPD distance/norm and general manifold suites: **2,137 passed, 310 skipped** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff passes.
- [Reproducible comparison and benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43845649936).

## Measured public-call performance

CPU, one thread, float64, PyTorch 2.6.0; median complete `check_point_on_manifold` time:

| Matrix shape | Requires gradient | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 × 16 | no | 0.0616 | 0.0555 | 1.11× |
| 128 × 128 | no | 1.2807 | 0.6873 | 1.86× |
| 512 × 512 | no | 38.3695 | 22.6112 | 1.70× |
| 1024 × 1024 | no | 234.0651 | 136.5331 | 1.71× |
| 1024 × 1024 | yes | 230.6996 | 141.3293 | 1.63× |
| 8 × 128 × 128 | yes | 10.4184 | 5.8600 | 1.78× |

These timings cover membership validation, not a complete optimization workload. GPU performance was not measured.

actual_prs.title: Apply line-search stabilization only to committed steps
actual_prs.head: a195aee07d4030ead58da6d54b9fb275bcaed6c6
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

`RiemannianLineSearch(stabilize=...)` projects leaf parameters with gradients enabled, so an otherwise successful optimization step raises an in-place autograd error. The stabilization counter and projection also run for `no_step=True` and unsuccessful searches, even though neither commits an update. Manual stabilization can additionally leave the cached gradient tied to the point before projection.

Run scheduled stabilization only after a committed step, perform projection without recording autograd operations, and invalidate cached gradients after projection. The next search then evaluates its closure at the stabilized point.

## Validation

- Unchanged upstream: **28 failures, 4 passing controls**.
- Real Sphere and CanonicalStiefel parameters with Armijo/Wolfe searches and stabilization periods 1/2; stabilization-disabled controls retain their behavior.
- Preview and rejected searches leave parameters bitwise unchanged and do not advance the stabilization interval, with and without an outer `no_grad` context.
- Manual stabilization preserves trainable leaf parameters and the next update matches a fresh gradient at the projected point.
- New regressions plus existing line-search, unused-parameter, trial-cache, and retraction-derivative suites: **166 passed** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff checks pass.
- [Reproducible original/candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43844769239).

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43845430580/job/133224287577) stops in `Setup Python 3.8`, before dependency installation or tests: Python 3.8 is unavailable on its Ubuntu 26.04 runner. The separate validation above uses Ubuntu 24.04 and checks this exact head on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0: **166 passed** per environment. These passing results do not change the failed upstream check status.

actual_prs.title: Preserve caller gradients when initializing scaled manifolds
actual_prs.head: fd3e256743cc73b9ca094e87312e4e3475f8c447
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

Constructing `Scaled` currently calls `requires_grad_(False)` on the tensor returned by `as_tensor`. With a caller-owned leaf tensor or Parameter, this silently disables gradients on that original object, including when the new manifold is learnable. With a non-leaf expression or a differentiable dtype conversion, construction raises instead.

Detach the initialization value without modifying the caller's tensor. Fixed scales remain non-differentiable buffers and learnable scales retain their own log-scale Parameter. This also allows initializing a nested scaled manifold from an existing learnable scale.

## Validation

- Unchanged upstream: **10 failures, 6 passing controls**.
- Regressions cover leaf tensors, Parameters, computed scales, differentiable dtype conversion, and both fixed/learnable initialization.
- A combined distance/training loss verifies caller gradients, point gradients, and the independently owned log-scale gradient.
- Nested scales preserve training of the inner manifold, and constant initialization/state-dict round trips remain unchanged.
- New tests plus existing scaling, manifold, and retraction-derivative suites: **2,124 passed, 310 skipped**, on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff checks pass.
- [Reproducible original/candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43842838144).

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43843496423/job/133217757136) stops in `Setup Python 3.8`, before dependency installation or tests: Python 3.8 is unavailable on its Ubuntu 26.04 runner. actual_prs.title: Preserve spherical subspaces with dependent spanning vectors
actual_prs.head: 27287337af8582524ebc603d8d9ff6ef675a97c5
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

A sphere intersection/complement is defined by the span of the supplied columns. Reduced QR nevertheless completes dependent columns with arbitrary orthogonal directions. Repeated, zero, or redundant spanning vectors therefore change the manifold: intersections gain unwanted directions and complements lose valid directions. Checking the rank of the already-built projector cannot recover the intended subspace.

Construct the orthogonal projector from the basis and its pseudoinverse, and validate the intended dimension from the basis rank. This supports dependent and overcomplete spanning sets and rejects zero- or one-dimensional subspaces, where the continuous sphere is empty or consists of isolated points.

## Validation

- Unchanged upstream: **28 failures, 4 passing controls**.
- Repeated/zero columns and overcomplete bases are checked against analytically known projectors for intersection/complement constraints, Sphere/SphereExact, and float32/float64.
- Random samples and projected tangent vectors remain in the intended span; batches can contain different valid ranks.
- Empty complements retain the unconstrained sphere. Full-rank projectors and their gradients match the QR formulation and pass finite-difference gradient checks.
- New tests plus existing spherical subspace, manifold, and Riemannian SGD suites: **2,210 passed, 310 skipped**, on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff checks pass.
- [Reproducible original/candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43842193798).

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43843375621/job/133217339827) stops in `Setup Python 3.8`, before dependency installation or tests: Python 3.8 is unavailable on its Ubuntu 26.04 runner. The separate validation above uses Ubuntu 24.04 and checks this exact head on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0: **2,210 passed, 310 skipped** per environment. These passing results do not change the failed upstream check status.

actual_prs.title: Avoid square intermediates in canonical Stiefel gradients
actual_prs.head: 784c5a0869fa7f0bda0af0f57749e17be1788e3a
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

Canonical Stiefel gradient conversion currently evaluates `(x @ u.T) @ x`. For an `n × m` Stiefel point this creates an `n × n` intermediate, even when only a small number of orthogonal columns is needed.

Associate the same product as `x @ (u.T @ x)`, so the inner product is only `m × m`. The formula and its derivatives are unchanged, while work falls from order `n²m` to `nm²`. This targets gradient conversion directly and is independent of the Cayley-retraction optimization in #307.

## Validation

- **30 new tests pass on both unchanged upstream and the candidate**: rectangular and square points, float32/float64, broadcast and empty batches, non-contiguous inputs, finite-difference gradients, canonical-metric duality, and complete SGD/Adam training trajectories against the original formula.
- New tests plus existing canonical Stiefel, manifold, Riemannian SGD and Adam suites: **2,246 passed, 310 skipped**, on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff checks pass.
- [Reproducible tests, timings and allocation measurements](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43841173703).

## Measured effect

CPU, float64, PyTorch 2.6.0, one thread; gradient-conversion medians:

| Shape | Forward, before → after | Forward + backward, before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 32 × 32 | 0.00712 → 0.00699 ms | 0.06061 → 0.06052 ms |
| 256 × 16 | 0.04877 → 0.01055 ms | 0.23041 → 0.07144 ms |
| 1,024 × 16 | 0.88336 → 0.03101 ms | 5.90624 → 0.14990 ms |
| 4 × 256 × 16 | 0.24140 → 0.03279 ms | 0.94285 → 0.17949 ms |

The 1,024 × 16 case is 28.49× faster forward and 39.40× faster with backward. Its largest individual matrix-product allocation, measured by the CPU profiler, falls from **8 MiB to 128 KiB**. These are kernel measurements; GPU and complete-training speedups have not been measured.

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43842003362/job/133212709045) stops in `Setup Python 3.8`, before dependency installation or tests: Python 3.8 is unavailable on its Ubuntu 26.04 runner. The [unchanged base job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43672079266/job/132684116427) fails for the same reason; the runner pin is already proposed in #300.

The separate validation above uses Ubuntu 24.04 and checks this exact head on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0: **2,246 passed, 310 skipped** per environment. These passing results do not change the failed upstream check status.

actual_prs.title: Keep Lorentz distances finite for large valid arguments
actual_prs.head: 7f09fb9fc2e828ac5679824c8aaad75b4dd320c5
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

The Lorentz distance kernel computes `acosh(x)` by squaring `x` before taking a square root. For valid finite float64 arguments above about `1.34e154`, that intermediate overflows even though the distance and its derivative are representable. For example, finite Lorentz exponential-map coordinates at distance 450 produce an infinite distance and non-finite gradients.

Evaluate the large-argument branch as `log(x) + log1p(sqrt(1 - 1/x²))`. Bound the inputs to both branches before selection so the inactive square cannot contaminate backward with overflow. The original regularized expression remains in use near the boundary, preserving its existing values and gradients at and below one.

## Validation

- The unchanged upstream fails **44 regressions**, while **14 controls pass**.
- Tests compare finite arguments through the largest float64 value against Python's `math.acosh` and an independently evaluated analytic derivative. They cover scalar and batched inputs.
- Boundary controls preserve values, gradients, and output dtype for float16, bfloat16, float32, and float64; finite-difference gradient checks cover both sides of the branch boundary.
- Public `expmap0(..., project=False)` → `dist0` and `dist` round trips cover distances corresponding to hyperbolic arguments 360, 450, and 600, three curvatures, both coordinate-axis positions, and `keepdim`; distances and derivatives remain finite.
- All new tests and existing Lorentz math, coordinates, axis, transport, and layer suites pass: **475 passed** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff checks pass.
- [Reproducible baseline and candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43839789228).

This change addresses the inverse-hyperbolic-cosine intermediate; the separate projection and general inner-product formulas are unchanged.

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43840620201/job/133208039563) stops in `Setup Python 3.8`, before dependency installation or tests: Python 3.8 is unavailable on its Ubuntu 26.04 runner. actual_prs.title: Reuse coalesced row gradients in sparse optimizers
actual_prs.head: 45f6f79216331db247fd22575ea95e5cc66c6b2d
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

Sparse embedding gradients already contain one sorted row index and one dense value row per entry after coalescing. Both sparse optimizers nevertheless find the unique rows again, select those same rows from the sparse tensor, and materialize the result.

Add a shared row-extraction fast path for this common hybrid COO layout. Reuse the coalesced indices and copy the value rows directly. The copy preserves caller-owned gradients when momentum or Nesterov modifies its working buffer. Fully coordinate-sparse COO gradients retain the existing extraction path.

## Validation

- **44 new tests pass on unchanged upstream and the candidate.** They compare both sparse layouts across SGD, momentum, Nesterov, Adam and AMSGrad; Euclidean and sphere parameters; minimize/maximize; duplicate and pre-coalesced rows; explicit zero gradient values; optimizer state; untouched parameter rows; and preservation of the input gradient.
- Real sparse Embedding backward/step sequences match PyTorch SGD and SparseAdam in float32 and float64. The Adam comparison uses a small positive epsilon in both implementations to isolate their differing epsilon placement.
- New tests plus all three existing sparse optimizer suites: **64 passed** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff checks pass.
- [Reproducible validation and benchmarks](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43839446704).

## Measured effect

CPU, PyTorch 2.6.0, float64, one thread, 50,000 × 64 parameters; complete optimizer `step()` medians after state initialization. Inputs contain duplicate rows, with either uncoalesced or pre-coalesced gradients.

| Optimizer | Input entries | Pre-coalesced | Before → after | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: |
| SGD | 128 | no | 0.1033 → 0.0507 ms | 2.04× |
| SGD | 128 | yes | 0.0696 → 0.0342 ms | 2.04× |
| SGD | 4096 | no | 2.2785 → 0.9852 ms | 2.31× |
| SGD | 4096 | yes | 0.8747 → 0.4125 ms | 2.12× |
| ADAM | 128 | no | 0.1709 → 0.1172 ms | 1.46× |
| ADAM | 128 | yes | 0.1368 → 0.1027 ms | 1.33× |
| ADAM | 4096 | no | 5.7678 → 4.3826 ms | 1.32× |
| ADAM | 4096 | yes | 3.6982 → 2.8577 ms | 1.29× |

These cases improve complete-step latency by 1.29–2.31×. GPU performance has not been measured.

actual_prs.title: Compute Takagi values without doubling the matrix dimension
actual_prs.head: d8898f1645ec66660631a0c52c0533220c9b97d0
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

`takagi_eigvals` is on every Siegel distance path. It currently builds a real `2n × 2n` compound matrix, computes all of its eigenvalues, then discards half of them. For a complex symmetric matrix, the required nonnegative Takagi values are its singular values.

Use `torch.linalg.svdvals` on the original `n × n` matrix and reverse its output to preserve ascending order. This avoids constructing the compound matrix and reduces the factorization dimension. The full `takagi_eig` factorization, which also returns vectors, is unchanged.

## Correctness and compatibility

- 61 new tests pass on both unchanged upstream and the candidate. They cover known spectra under independently constructed unitary congruences, zero/repeated values, scales `1e-7` through `1e7`, complex64/complex128, batched and empty inputs, ascending order, and gradients along symmetric directions.
- Finite-difference `gradcheck` and the original compound-matrix formula independently check derivatives.
- New tests plus the complete existing Takagi and Siegel-distance suites: **4,411 passed** on both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. Ruff checks pass.
- [Reproducible tests and benchmarks](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43836674552).

## Measured effect

CPU, PyTorch 2.6.0, complex128, one thread; `torch.utils.benchmark` medians:

| Workload | Before → after, forward | Before → after, forward + backward |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Takagi values, 16 × 32 × 32 | 1.705 → 0.824 ms | 4.118 → 2.530 ms |
| Takagi values, 4 × 128 × 128 | 8.894 → 5.071 ms | 18.803 → 10.501 ms |
| Takagi values, 1 × 256 × 256 | 10.825 → 6.344 ms | 25.030 → 14.187 ms |
| Full bounded-domain distance, 4 × 64 × 64 | 5.125 → 4.389 ms | 9.642 → 8.502 ms |
| Full bounded-domain distance, 1 × 128 × 128 | 6.148 → 5.230 ms | 11.993 → 10.523 ms |

The internal operation is 1.71–2.07× faster forward and 1.63–1.79× faster with backward in these cases; the complete distance is 1.13–1.18× faster. GPU performance has not been measured.

The same setup failure is present on the unchanged upstream base in [run 43672079266](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43672079266). Existing PR #300 addresses the runner selection separately.

For this exact head `d8898f1645ec66660631a0c52c0533220c9b97d0`, [run 43836674552](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43836674552) uses Ubuntu 24.04 and passes the 61 new tests on unchanged upstream, then all 4,411 selected tests on the candidate, in both Python 3.8/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.6.0. actual_prs.title: Reduce dense products in Siegel inner products
actual_prs.head: d1ea20de7503e688f3b37b32b92845a9c101a221
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

Siegel inner products currently construct inverse matrices and multiply complete square matrices even though the result needs only a trace. This adds cubic work to both the bounded-domain and upper-half metrics.

Compute the trace as an elementwise contraction of the two scaled tangent vectors. Norm calculations reuse one scaled vector; the bounded model uses direct solves and avoids constructing either inverse. Upper-half cross products reuse the existing real inverse so that two complex factorizations do not make that path slower. The metric factor order, complex output dtype, broadcasting, and existing `keepdim` shape are preserved.

## Correctness

- 68 new cases pass against the original inverse formula on unchanged upstream and on the candidate, including complex64/complex128, complementary batch axes, both models, norm/cross products, and `keepdim`.
- Independent inverse-formula gradients and finite-difference `gradcheck` cover both models and both norm/cross paths.
- The new tests plus the existing manifold suite pass: **2,158 passed, 310 skipped**. Ruff checks pass.
- [Reproducible baseline/candidate tests and measurements](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43835397300/job/133190629261).

## Measured performance

CPU, PyTorch 2.6.0, complex128, one thread; medians from `torch.utils.benchmark` at batch/size `(16,32)`, `(4,128)`, and `(1,256)`:

| Operation | Forward speedup | Forward + backward speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Bounded-domain cross product | 1.57–1.88× | 1.11–1.76× |
| Bounded-domain squared norm | 2.36–2.64× | 1.75–2.76× |
| Upper-half cross product | 1.19–1.47× | 1.21–1.40× |
| Upper-half squared norm, sizes 128–256 | 1.68–1.70× | 1.74–2.10× |

The small upper-half squared-norm forward case is a tradeoff: 0.566 → 0.623 ms (about 10% slower), while its forward+backward case improves from 1.695 → 1.440 ms. GPU performance has not been measured.

Existing PR #300 addresses the runner selection separately.

actual_prs.title: Reduce intermediate products in Euclidean Stiefel exponential maps
actual_prs.head: 78c37b66257412094c6cc6d54d58bd55c4044947
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

The Euclidean Stiefel exponential map first multiplies the tall `[x, u]` matrix by a full `2m × 2m` exponential, then multiplies the result by a selector whose bottom half is zero. This computes intermediate columns that do not contribute to the output.

Take the first `m` exponential columns and compose their small right factor before applying the tall matrix. This reduces the intermediate tall product and avoids materializing the zero selector, while preserving the same exponential-map formula and its derivatives. `EuclideanStiefelExact` uses the optimized map through its existing aliases.

## Validation

[Unchanged-base and exact-candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43832953919):

- All **15 new tests** pass on both versions. They compare with the full block formula, check float32/float64, batched and square/tall inputs, manifold membership, zero steps, curve initial velocity, and the exact-retraction alias.
- Finite-difference checks cover derivatives of both the point and tangent; their gradients also agree with the full formula.
- The new tests and existing manifold suite pass: **2,105 passed, 310 skipped**.
- Ruff passes.

Single-thread CPU float64, PyTorch 2.6.0:

| Batch × rows × columns | Forward before / after | Forward + backward before / after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 × 128 × 8 | 0.363 / 0.352 ms | 1.811 / 1.784 ms |
| 4 × 512 × 16 | 0.538 / 0.480 ms | 2.689 / 2.507 ms |
| 1 × 2048 × 16 | 0.491 / 0.437 ms | 1.990 / 1.545 ms |
| 4 × 32 × 16 | 0.304 / 0.307 ms | 1.587 / 1.599 ms |

The two taller 16-column cases improve by about 12% in forward speed, with 7–29% improvement in forward-plus-backward speed. The near-square control is approximately unchanged (about 1% slower in this run). The workflow records timing dispersion; GPU performance has not been measured.

SPD parallel transport computes the square root of a whitened positive-definite matrix as `exp(0.5 * log(M))`. After the spectral logarithm, that also evaluates a dense matrix exponential and its derivative.

## Validation

- The new tests and existing SPD-distance/manifold suites pass: **2,133 passed, 310 skipped**.
- Ruff passes.
- Profiling verifies that the two eigendecompositions remain, while matrix-exponential calls drop from one to zero for forward evaluation and from two to zero for forward plus backward.

| Batch × matrix size | Forward before / after | Forward + backward before / after |
| --- | --- | --- |

| 4 × 128 | 28.906 / 21.775 ms | 123.896 / 42.140 ms |

Both Siegel Cayley transforms explicitly invert a matrix and then multiply by that inverse. These transforms are used when mapping between the bounded-domain and upper-half models, including bounded-domain sampling and distance calculations.

actual_prs.title: Use low-rank Cayley solves for tall Stiefel matrices
actual_prs.head: 2846064db5d6d637cf683167fc257507d301a8af
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

Canonical Stiefel retraction and transport build and factor an `n x n` Cayley matrix even when the point has only `m` columns. For tall orthogonal weights this makes the update much more expensive than its low-rank structure requires.

When `2m < n`, apply the same Cayley transform through its rank-`2m` factors and the Woodbury identity. The solve is `2m x 2m`, and the implementation does not construct the dense `n x n` matrix. This covers `retr`, `transp_follow_retr`, and their combined operation. The existing dense path remains in use when `2m >= n`.

The rank factors retain the corrected tangent velocity introduced in #280 and preserve the retraction and transport equations.

## Validation

[Validation and benchmark run](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43823774649), using PyTorch 2.6.0 CPU, Python 3.12, float64, and one thread:

- All **19 new numerical tests pass on both unchanged upstream and the candidate**. They compare against the full dense Cayley equations, verify orthogonality, transported tangency and metric preservation, and compare derivatives with respect to all three inputs. They also cover a zero step, initial velocity, float32, batch broadcasting, noncontiguous inputs, empty batches, and the dense fallback.
- The candidate plus existing manifold, canonical Stiefel, retraction-derivative, SGD and Adam suites have **2,207 passed, 310 skipped**.
- Ruff passes.

Measured combined `retr_transp` medians, including construction and the solve:

| Shape (batch, n, m) | Forward before → after | Forward + backward before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (8, 64, 4) | 0.275 → 0.092 ms | 0.923 → 0.418 ms |
| (4, 256, 8) | 2.456 → 0.129 ms | 7.176 → 0.671 ms |
| (1, 1024, 16) | 16.497 → 0.295 ms | 37.149 → 1.322 ms |

The profiler confirms coefficient matrices shrink from 64/256/1024 square to 8/16/32 square in these cases. A (2, 64, 32) control still uses the original 64-square solve and has essentially unchanged combined-operation timing. These are CPU measurements on this runner, not a promise for every device or shape; the full 16-case timings, interquartile ranges and test reports are attached to the validation run.

## Scope and history

This is independent of the earlier QR-autograd repair (#290) and the separate combined-transport batch-shape proposal: neither changes the Cayley linear system. The upstream patch contains the implementation and numerical tests; the benchmark workflow is confined to the validation branch.

actual_prs.title: Initialize sparse SGD momentum from the first tangent gradient
actual_prs.head: a86617d9f6cd92dd723dabd40e6666e5362f0982
actual_prs.body:
## Problem and change

Sparse SGD initializes its momentum buffer from the raw Euclidean gradient and immediately applies the recurrence again after converting the gradient to the manifold's tangent space. With momentum 0.9 and no dampening, the first Euclidean update is 1.9 times the expected SGD step. On a sphere, a normal component can also enter the first update.

Initialize the selected rows of a new parameter's momentum buffer from its first Riemannian gradient. Later sparse updates keep the existing lazy-row recurrence and checkpoint layout. A previously inactive row still follows that later recurrence; initialization is per parameter, not per row.

## Validation

Fifteen deterministic regressions cover real sparse embedding gradients with duplicate indices, four-step comparisons with native PyTorch SGD, float32/float64, momentum, dampening, Nesterov, maximize, independently calculated spherical retractions, delayed parameters, delayed rows, inactive-row preservation and checkpoint continuation.

The [exact-candidate workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43816577279/job/133129886156) checks out this PR's commit, substitutes only the unchanged upstream implementation for the baseline, and restores the candidate for the passing run:

- Same new tests on unchanged upstream: **11 failed, 4 passed**.
- New regressions plus the complete existing sparse SGD, sparse Adam and dense first-momentum modules: **31 passed**. This retains the original 2,000-step Poincaré convergence tests.
- Changed-file Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

Linux, Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.6.0+cpu. GPU execution and the full repository suite were not run.

## Related work

#254 corrected first momentum initialization in dense `RiemannianSGD`; its changed files do not include `sparse_rsgd.py`. This addresses the separate sparse execution path. Checked all 182 prior upstream PR file lists and the nine patches that touch this implementation, plus both source variants across the fork branches; none contains this sparse initialization fix.

## Official CI follow-up

The [upstream job](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43817013811/job/133131261358) stops while installing Python 3.8 on Ubuntu 26.04, before dependency installation, lint, or tests. The same setup error is present in the [base-branch run](https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt/actions/runs/43672079266) at `4623ea1d2a9808b8e87bf10949cccb2c5ec6233c`; the runner-image fix is already proposed separately in #300.

I also checked this PR's exact head, `a86617d9f6cd92dd723dabd40e6666e5362f0982`, on Ubuntu 24.04 with **Python 3.8 and PyTorch 2.0.1 CPU**. Its new tests and neighboring suites pass: **20 passed**. [Reproducible minimum-version validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43833874420/job/133185533699). The earlier current-version correctness and benchmark evidence above remains applicable.

actual_prs.title: Preserve quoted MCP launch arguments and reject incomplete commands
actual_prs.body:
## Problem

The launch-command tokenizer drops empty quoted arguments and removes backslashes that are literal inside single quotes or before ordinary characters in double quotes. This changes the argv passed to the MCP server: an empty option value can consume the next option, and a quoted path can point to the wrong file.

The raw shell-operator check also rejects quoted dependency constraints. The existing Trading Research Agents entry uses `uvx --with "mcp>=2,<3" trading-research-agents mcp serve`, but its configuration currently falls back to a placeholder.

## Change

Check shell operators during tokenization so quoted or escaped punctuation remains literal while unquoted `;`, `&`, `|`, `<`, and `>` are rejected. The regression cases cover all four clients, unsafe-operator controls, and configuration generation from the existing Trading Research Agents catalog entry.

actual_prs.name: registry-invalid-request-target
actual_prs.title: Reject malformed HTTP targets without terminating the registry API
actual_prs.body:
## Problem

The HTTP handler constructs a `URL` before entering its error handler. A malformed request target such as `//[` or `http://localhost:bad` throws from that constructor, escapes the async request callback, and terminates the API process under Node's default unhandled-rejection behavior. The failed request can therefore interrupt unrelated clients.

## Change

Catch URL-construction errors at the request boundary and return the existing JSON error format with status 400. Route dispatch remains unchanged for valid targets.

The regressions launch the real API in an isolated child process, send four malformed targets over HTTP, check the 400 response, and then check `/health` in the **same process**. This exercises process survival without changing global rejection handling or relying on a mocked URL parser.

## Validation

Tested the exact independent commit on Node.js 20, 22, and 24. All **4** new HTTP regressions fail against unchanged production code. actual_prs.body:
## Problem

The API entrypoint constructs a file URL by concatenating `file://` with a filesystem path. A checkout path containing `#`, `?`, or literal percent escapes is interpreted as URL syntax, so the direct-run comparison fails and the production API exits without starting.

## Change

Convert `import.meta.url` to a filesystem path with `fileURLToPath` before comparing it to the resolved entrypoint path.

## Change

## Validation

It checks result limits, ranked and unfiltered ordering, exact ties, filters, and unchanged input order. A Node.js 20 benchmark uses the real **9,846-entry catalog**, five query forms, and limits 1, 5, 25, and 100. All 20 result sets have exactly the same serialized summaries before and after. Each measurement uses five warmup calls, then five samples of ten calls.

actual_prs.title: Resolve omitted timestamps consistently in EKF and UKF
actual_prs.head: 8cf3dc4d4cfdba7d049cac81fcf022c298a3b6a2
actual_prs.body:
Fixes #519.

## Problem and change

When `t` is omitted, NLS reference-point selection uses the current system clock, but EKF and UKF pass `None` to the actual transition and observation methods. A time-dependent model can fail during prediction, or evaluate prediction at a different time from its Jacobian.

Resolve the default timestamp once at the start of each update and pass that value through the existing calculations. Copy the current clock so a later reset cannot invalidate a saved backward value. Explicit timestamps retain their existing behavior. The production change is one line in each filter.

## Validation

Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu:

- New tests on unchanged main `298e9f0862cb228b0e8851b2616e682ccdca6a32`: **18 failed, 14 passed**.
- New tests plus existing EKF, UKF and dynamics suites: **50 passed**.
- Complete `python -m pytest -q`: **432 passed, 18 skipped**. The skips cover unavailable CUDA and the optional sparse backend.
- `git diff --check` passes.

The regressions compare actual posterior states and covariances with an independent scalar Kalman reference in float32/float64. They cover models that require a timestamp, models with their own `None` fallback, explicit overrides, repeated clock changes, time-independent controls and backward after resetting the model clock.

This targets the filters' direct model evaluations. #516 addresses saved timestamps inside NLS itself; #440 addresses independent-batch Jacobians. Neither contains this default-time resolution.

actual_prs.title: Preserve independent EPnP directions when eigenvectors become complex
actual_prs.head: 020e8f5d08a890d446bd42bfab58d381ade694a1
actual_prs.body:
Closes #520.

## Problem

EPnP computes eigenvectors of the real symmetric Gram matrix with the general eigensolver, then discards their imaginary parts. Near repeated small eigenvalues, a complex-conjugate pair can become two identical real directions. The four selected vectors then have rank three, which can corrupt the pose estimate even for a valid scene with all points in front of the camera.

The five-point float32 example in #520 has mean reprojection error **481.06 px without refinement and 598.10 px with refinement** on the unchanged base. With this change, the errors are approximately **0.00070 px and 0.00015 px**, respectively.

## Change

Detect non-real selected eigenvectors and recompute only those batch members with the real symmetric eigensolver. Keep the existing real basis, reverse eigenvalue ordering and gather layout for ordinary members.

An unconditional eigensolver replacement was tested and rejected because another valid basis changed beta initialization and regressed two previously successful four-point refinements. This narrower fallback preserves those controls. Beta coefficient ordering and input broadcasting are unchanged.

## Validation

Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu:

- The focused regression suite has **14 failures and 19 passing controls** on unchanged main; **33 pass** with the fix.
- Check basis rank and the invariant subspace against an independently constructed projective matrix and its SVD, across float32/float64, 4/5/9 points and multiple batch axes.
- Exercise public EPnP with and without refinement, the two successful four-point controls, mixed normal/affected batches, requested subspace widths, and finite nonzero gradients for scalar and mixed batches.
- A separate 96-scene comparison across 4/5/6/12 points and both dtypes reduces rank-deficient selections from **22 to 0**. No case with original reprojection error below 0.01 px exceeds 0.1 px after the fix. This is a measured regression sample, not a guarantee for every degenerate camera geometry.
- Complete repository suite: **433 passed, 18 skipped**. The skipped cases require unavailable CUDA or optional BAE dependencies.
- `git diff --check` passes.

All 329 prior PR diffs, 53 pre-existing fork branches, and all 134 reachable commits touching the PnP implementation were checked for an earlier equivalent change.

actual_prs.title: Normalize vector CG initial guesses to the internal column shape
actual_prs.head: c2cfac575d728fb47a966df4e9a1c66b00793c09
actual_prs.body:
Closes #523.

CG converts a vector right-hand side into a column internally, but leaves an explicitly supplied vector initial guess unchanged. Even a zero guess or the exact solution then fails with an incompatible broadcast in the residual or in-place update.

Normalize a supplied vector guess to the same internal column representation. The recurrence, convergence policy, existing column output shape and supplied-column behavior remain unchanged. This is independent of #460's handling of already-converged batch members.

## Validation

On Python 3.12.14 / PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu:

- Unchanged main: **30 failures and 18 passing controls**.
- Fixed focused suite: **48 passed**, using float32/float64 and dense, COO, CSR and BSR matrices.
- Zero, nonzero and exact vector initial guesses are compared with independent direct solves and the original linear equation. Passing controls cover no initial guess and explicit column guesses.
- Additional cases exercise preconditioning, noncontiguous initial guesses, zero right-hand sides and identical batched systems without changing the existing batch-convergence algorithm.
- Full repository suite: **448 passed, 18 skipped**. Skips require unavailable CUDA or optional BAE dependencies.
- `git diff --check` passes.

The 329 prior PR diffs, 53 pre-existing fork branches and all reachable historical solver implementations were checked. None normalizes a supplied vector guess to the current column representation.

actual_prs.title: Use half-open cumulative intervals when resampling particles
actual_prs.head: d10c24fe0292df3f66dd2b8351e56c62139c6d2e
actual_prs.body:
Closes #524.

Particle resampling documents the interval `cdf[j-1] <= r < cdf[j]`, but the current left insertion assigns an exact boundary draw to the previous interval. A draw of zero can therefore select a particle with zero probability. Native float16 draws with the seeded example in #524 select three zero-weight particles out of 4,096 even though only one particle has positive weight.

Use right insertion in the cumulative distribution lookup. The batch-axis handling, endpoint clamp and random draw count are unchanged.

## Validation

On Python 3.12.14 / PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu:

- Unchanged main: **14 failures and 2 passing controls**.
- Fixed focused suite: **16 passed**.
- Deterministic float32/float64 draws check the documented half-open intervals, including leading and internal zero-weight intervals, positive cumulative boundaries, multiple batch axes and different distributions in one batch.
- Native seeded float16/bfloat16 sampling verifies that no zero-weight particle is selected. These low-precision cases exercise the resampling helper rather than claiming support for complete CPU half-precision covariance factorization.
- Interior-draw controls retain their existing assignments.
- Full repository suite: **416 passed, 18 skipped**. Skips require unavailable CUDA or optional BAE dependencies.
- `git diff --check` passes.

All historical PF implementations reachable from the 329 prior PRs and 53 pre-existing fork branches retain left insertion. This correction is distinct from #352's batch-axis and CDF-endpoint work.

actual_prs.title: Preserve FastTriggs kernel ownership across copies and checkpoints
actual_prs.head: d40393ed5234f358a55bd3edf643b4aa0cd23dad
actual_prs.body:
Closes #527.

## Problem

FastTriggs captures its kernel only in a constructor-local lambda. A deep copy keeps that callable bound to the original kernel, so changing the original silently changes the copy's corrections. Parameters and buffers of a stateful kernel are also missing from the corrector's module tree, dtype/device conversion and state dictionary. Serializing an ordinary Huber corrector fails because the local lambda cannot be pickled.

This affects actual optimization: after copying a Huber corrector and changing the original kernel, a simple outlier-fitting Gauss–Newton step becomes approximately **0.08264** instead of the independent copy's expected **0.32258**.

## Change

Register the kernel as a normal child module and use a bound method to sum its output for the Jacobian callback. Preserve the correction equations and the existing `func(x)` callable behavior.

## Validation

Python 3.12.14 / PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu:

- Unchanged main: **13 failures and 6 passing controls**.
- Fixed focused suite: **19 passed**.
- Independent deep copies for Huber and Cauchy; full serialization round trips for Huber, Cauchy and Scale; stateful-kernel parameter/buffer restoration and float64 conversion.
- An actual Gauss–Newton optimization step agrees with its analytic weighted least-squares solution after the original kernel is mutated.
- Existing corrections agree with independent analytic kernel weights in float32 and float64.
- Complete repository suite: **419 passed, 18 skipped**. Skips require unavailable CUDA or optional BAE dependencies.
- `git diff --check` passes.

All 43 reachable historical commits affecting correctors, including intermediate source versions, retain the lambda capture. This does not change the inference-mode policy or Triggs' second-derivative handling.

actual_prs.title: Encode unseen NumEncoder categories without dtype errors or collisions
actual_prs.head: 199a65d74bfd856d381adc9bd977e454d5c1df9d

actual_prs.title: Project only the needed KCNN knowledge embeddings for small batches
actual_prs.head: a8c132ba9975becd2d2bf74ae491cb432527bffa
actual_prs.body:
### Description

KCNN currently projects and applies `tanh` to the entire entity/context vocabulary before looking up a batch's rows. A batch with 40 entity positions therefore transforms two 10,000-row tables. Gather the fixed embeddings first when the batch has fewer positions than the vocabulary; otherwise retain full-table projection. Entity and context channels choose independently.

`embedding_tables()` remains unchanged, so whole-vocabulary embedding regularization retains its meaning. Tests check the computation bound, float32/float64 outputs and parameter gradients, repeated/noncontiguous IDs, optional channels, unused entities in regularization, and a complete DKN optimizer step followed by evaluation.

### Measured CPU effect

The [reproducible benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/blob/validation/recommenders-kcnn-20261116/.validation/benchmark_kcnn.py) uses PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu, one thread, the same model weights/storage for both implementations, five warmups and alternating measurement order. | Workload | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| KCNN forward, 10k entities, 4 x 10 positions | 1.655 ms | 0.239 ms | 6.92x |

All five evaluation metrics match; KCNN maximum output difference is zero in these benchmark cases.

actual_prs.title: Keep SLi-Rec attention padding representable in float16
actual_prs.head: 9cdeeb972c7909405ca9ff32778ca98baa0441f6
actual_prs.body:
### Description

SLi-Rec's masked attention constructs the TensorFlow-era sentinel `-(2**32)+1` in the score dtype. It cannot be represented in float16, so `full_like` raises before masking even for an entirely valid history. A complete SLi-Rec forward pass under CPU float16 autocast also fails.

Bound this finite sentinel by the score dtype's minimum finite value. Float32, float64 and bfloat16 retain the existing sentinel; float16 uses its representable lower bound. The existing fully padded-row behavior remains finite and unchanged.

Fixes #2450.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43907660754) checks exact head `9cdeeb972c7909405ca9ff32778ca98baa0441f6` against unchanged staging:

- Python 3.10 with the declared PyTorch 2.0.1 minimum: **22 passed, 4 skipped**. Independent tiny operator probes confirm that this version lacks the CPU half linear/autocast support required by those four cases. Supported dtype cases run normally.
- Tests cover float16/bfloat16/float32/float64 with empty, partial and full masks, plus complete SLi-Rec autocast forward, backward and optimizer steps.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 reproduces the same four failures and passes all 26 patched tests.

### History review

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads, 69 existing fork branches and all 15 reachable SLi-Rec source versions, including previous TensorFlow paths, the former `sli_rec_pytorch.py` filename and intermediate commits. This fix is limited to attention sentinel representability.

actual_prs.title: Compute SLi-Rec pairwise loss in log space
actual_prs.head: 53f279ab4469b8e2a9b5185dfaa9c623e3c4169f
actual_prs.body:
### Description

The pairwise loss computes `softmax` and then `log`. A sufficiently low-scoring positive rounds to zero probability before the logarithm, producing an infinite loss and NaN gradients. This occurs in a complete SLi-Rec training example with finite logits, not only in a standalone loss calculation.

Use `log_softmax` directly and retain the existing positive-label mask and group normalization. Finite log probabilities remain available even when the corresponding probability would underflow.

Fixes #2451.

### Validation

actual_prs.title: Keep xDeepFM norm gradients finite at zero residuals and filters
actual_prs.head: a19e80dafb707cd6abb30de08b80da6dbf3040f1
actual_prs.body:
### Description

xDeepFM expresses both RMSE and CIN Frobenius regularization as a square root of a sum of squares. At an exact fit or an all-zero CIN filter, the forward value is valid but the composed backward produces NaN gradients. An optimizer step can consequently corrupt otherwise finite model parameters.

Compute these objectives with `torch.linalg.vector_norm`, which selects a finite zero subgradient at the origin. Divide the residual norm by the square root of the element count to preserve RMSE. The CIN term still uses the Frobenius norm of the entire filter. Both occurrences of this zero-norm issue are handled together.

Fixes #2452.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43887605963) checks exact head `a19e80dafb707cd6abb30de08b80da6dbf3040f1` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- Unchanged xDeepFM, FFM dataset and shared FCN suites: **35 passed**.
- New regressions on unchanged staging: **10 failed, 4 passing controls**.
- Patched suites: **49 passed** in both environments.
- Tests cover float32/float64, regression/classification exact fits, one/two CIN layers, independent nonzero RMSE and 3-4-5 norm gradient references, and complete model Adam steps for both zero-norm cases.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 gives the same results.

### History review

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads and 69 existing fork branches, including all 6 reachable PyTorch xDeepFM versions, 22 former TensorFlow xDeepFM versions and 102 shared base-model versions, with intermediate and former-path commits included.

### Checklist

- [x] Contribution guidelines and code style followed.
- [x] Regression tests added to the existing registered model test module.
- [x] Comments explain the numerical choice; public API is unchanged.
- [x] Commits include the required `Signed-off-by` trailer.
- [x] Targets `staging`.

The upstream [job log](https://github.com/recommenders-team/recommenders/actions/runs/43888820974/job/133374249182) records an environment setup failure. The Python 3.10 CPU/Spark job stopped while building its Docker image: adding the deadsnakes PPA raised `http.client.IncompleteRead` before Python installation or project tests ran. The other matrix jobs were cancelled. Independent validation of the exact contribution head is linked above.

actual_prs.title: Use the latest observed time in SLi-Rec preference fusion
actual_prs.head: a9147aa957d9793832899e1285febfe95eae77a0
actual_prs.body:
### Description

The adaptive preference-fusion gate reads `time_to_now[:, -1:]`, but the dataset left-aligns history and pads the remaining columns. Short histories therefore supply a padded zero instead of the interval since the latest real behavior. With two observations and a three-day gap, the gate receives `log(3)` at maximum length 2 and zero at maximum length 5.

Use the existing sequence length to gather the last observed time, and supply a neutral zero for an empty history. Full and truncated histories keep their existing temporal context. The correction changes the fusion feature only; checkpoint parameter shapes are unchanged.

Fixes #2456.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43896904939) checks exact head `a9147aa957d9793832899e1285febfe95eae77a0` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.10–3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- Unchanged SLi-Rec suite: **12 passed**.
- New cases on the baseline: **7 failed, 8 passing controls**.
- Patched model suite: **27 passed**.
- Native dataset tests cover short/full/truncated histories, maximum length one, and positive/negative sample groups. Additional cases cover mixed and empty masks and noncontiguous time tensors.
- Complete float32/float64 model predictions, parameter gradients and Adam updates match a separate row-wise reference that selects the last observed event.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 gives the same results.

### References and history

The [SLi-Rec paper, section 3.3](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2019/0585.pdf) uses temporal context to adapt preference fusion and evaluates the interval since a user's last behavior. This patch restores the observed interval as the fusion input.

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads, 69 existing fork branches and all 15 reachable SLi-Rec source versions, including former TensorFlow paths, the former `sli_rec_pytorch.py` filename and intermediate commits. All historical variants select the final padded column.

- [x] The code comment explains the padding/recency distinction.
- [x] Commit includes the required `Signed-off-by` trailer.

actual_prs.title: Select sequential checkpoints using the validation metric direction
actual_prs.head: 201ca1ac15ae441749a7fad848cdb0a089f97a0d
actual_prs.body:
### Description

The sequential trainer treats every validation metric as higher-is-better. Choosing `logloss` or `rmse` therefore saves the model with the largest error and can stop when that error decreases. A real SLi-Rec run selects epoch 3 (logloss 0.7067) although epoch 1 has the lowest observed error (0.7017).

Minimize the two supported error metrics and continue maximizing ranking/accuracy metrics. Initialize the comparison with the corresponding infinity so a valid zero score can establish the first checkpoint. Checkpoint selection and early-stopping patience use the same comparison. Document the metric direction in `fit`.

Fixes #2457.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43891129363) checks exact head `201ca1ac15ae441749a7fad848cdb0a089f97a0d` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- New cases on unchanged staging: **8 failed, 3 passing controls**.
- Patched model suite: **23 passed**.
- Controlled metric trajectories verify direction, zero scores, ties, non-improving NaN scores, patience and exact saved weights while the training loop performs real forward/backward/Adam steps.
- Separate integration cases calculate actual logloss, RMSE and AUC during three training epochs, independently find the optimum, reload the saved checkpoint and reproduce its validation score.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 gives the same results.

### History review

These variants initialize `best_metric=0` and maximize every evaluation metric; intermediate commits and former paths are included.

actual_prs.title: Skip shared padding in the SLi-Rec recurrent scan
actual_prs.head: 747087a8b6cef54a0bdc8545bc3d3bd31148f3c5
actual_prs.body:
### Description

The Time4LSTM driver executes every padded step, even after all histories in a batch have ended. A batch whose longest history has seven events still performs 50 cell calls at the default maximum length.

Stop recurrent work at the longest valid history and append a zero output tail. Keep one differentiable step for all-padding batches so input and parameter gradients remain zero tensors. Output shape, parameter layout and the full-width behavior for dense or empty batches are preserved.

Fixes #2460.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43893999137) checks exact head `747087a8b6cef54a0bdc8545bc3d3bd31148f3c5` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- Unchanged SLi-Rec suite: **12 passed**.
- New cases on unchanged staging: **11 failed, 6 passing controls**.
- Patched model suite: **29 passed** in both environments.
- Float32/float64 tests compare outputs and input/parameter gradients with the original full-width unroll, including mixed lengths, all padding, noncontiguous views, dense histories and empty batches.
- Complete model predictions, binary cross-entropy gradients, Adam updates and file-evaluation metrics match the reference.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass.

### Measured effect

Local CPU, Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1, one thread, five warmups and 31 alternating samples per version:

| Workload | Unchanged staging | Bounded scan | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cell forward, 32 rows, 7 valid / 50 padded steps | 10.25 ms | 1.49 ms | 6.88x |
| Cell forward and backward, same batch | 54.93 ms | 10.01 ms | 5.49x |
| Complete file evaluation, 40 examples, maximum 7 / 50 steps | 38.76 ms | 27.87 ms | 1.39x |
| Dense 50 / 50 forward control | 10.39 ms | 10.49 ms | 0.99x |
| Dense 50 / 50 forward/backward control | 50.88 ms | 51.32 ms | 0.99x |

The complete evaluation includes the dataset, model, attention and seven ranking/classification metrics; all reported metrics are unchanged. Dense controls were about 1% slower in this measurement. Determining the bound reads the maximum sequence length once; CUDA timings were not measured. The validation workflow includes the benchmark script and results as artifacts.

### History review

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads and 69 existing fork branches, including both reachable Time4LSTM driver versions under the current and former `rnn_cell_pytorch.py` filenames and their intermediate commits. Both execute the full padded width.

actual_prs.title: Preserve sequential ranking groups across evaluation batches
actual_prs.head: 8325924934e574c081031cf8be91bfe24f5a720c
actual_prs.body:
### Description

Sequential evaluation reshapes each inference batch into ranking groups. A valid file containing one positive and four negatives per group therefore fails with batch sizes such as 8 or 32, because a group crosses the batch boundary. The same error interrupts validation inside `fit`.

Collect predictions and labels in file order, then form the ranking groups once all batches are available. This keeps group membership independent of the inference batch size. Aligned-batch metrics remain unchanged, and incomplete input files still raise instead of silently discarding rows.

Fixes #2462.

### Validation

- Two integration cases perform real training and parameter updates, then validate with unaligned training batch sizes.
- Additional cases cover whole-group history filtering and rejection of a truncated final group.

actual_prs.title: Preserve RLRMC ratings for repeated pairs and low-memory prediction
actual_prs.head: f74abf8dffada2f9f4b70286fd043aba4fd12b04
actual_prs.body:
### Description

RLRMC trains on mean-centered ratings. Its low-memory prediction path subtracts the training mean, while its sparse path adds the mean only correctly for unique pairs. Repeated coordinates are combined by CSR construction, which accumulates their offsets and leaves some requested output entries unwritten. A factor score of 10 with training mean 3 consequently returns 7 in low-memory mode and `[16, -3]` for two identical pairs in sparse mode.

Restore the mean in both paths. Score sorted unique pairs with the existing sparse Numba kernel, then map the scores back to every original occurrence. Repeated and unsorted requests now preserve their order and multiplicity, and empty requests return an empty float64 array. This retains sparse scoring without gathering a dense factor array for every requested pair.

Fixes #2464.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43899465242) checks exact head `f74abf8dffada2f9f4b70286fd043aba4fd12b04` against unchanged staging using the Pymanopt revision documented in `setup.py`:

- Python 3.11: NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.13.1, Numba 0.61.2.
- Existing GeoIMC experimental controls: **12 passed**.
- New tests on unchanged RLRMC: **17 failed, 11 passing controls**.
- Patched RLRMC and GeoIMC suites: **40 passed**, with no skips, in both environments.
- Cases cover positive, negative and zero training means; string IDs; noncontiguous factors; unique, interleaved and repeated pairs; batch partitioning; empty and mismatched inputs.
- Four integration cases run native RLRMC training with and without centering and compare both prediction modes to an independent factor-sum reference.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14 gives the same results.

### History review

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads and 69 pre-existing fork branches, including 14 RLRMC algorithm source versions from 85 reachable commits under current and former paths. None contains an equivalent prediction correction. The earlier fork change to RLRMC dataset column names concerns data preprocessing and is separate from pair scoring.

actual_prs.title: Keep DKN item-to-item normalization finite in low precision
actual_prs.head: eb6af96ae54feacc80b31fd3cb71869a55edc1ad
actual_prs.body:
### Description

DKN item-to-item normalization squares article embeddings and applies its `1e-12` floor in the embedding dtype. In float16 the floor rounds to zero, so zero embeddings become NaN; small nonzero embeddings can also underflow during squaring. Native KCNN outputs then contaminate relation scores and the training loss, including under CPU float16 autocast.

Compute normalization in float32 for float16/bfloat16 embeddings, then return the original dtype. This preserves the squared-norm floor and zero-vector convention. Float32 and float64 keep the existing calculation exactly.

Fixes #2466.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43902450955) checks exact head `eb6af96ae54feacc80b31fd3cb71869a55edc1ad` against unchanged staging:

- Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1: existing DKN, item-to-item and dataset suites **71 passed, 1 CUDA-only skip**; new regressions on the baseline **6 failed, 10 passing controls**; patched suites **87 passed, 1 CUDA-only skip**.
- Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1: **80 passed, 8 skipped** after the patch. One skip is the existing CUDA test; seven new float16 CPU cases require native linear/autocast capabilities absent from this version. An independent tiny operator probe confirms that limitation.
- Four dtypes and zero, small and ordinary embeddings are checked against a float64 vector-norm reference. Float32/float64 results additionally match the former expression exactly.
- Complete native KCNN/document-transform/relation-score paths run forward, backward and SGD updates with explicit half parameters and CPU half autocast. Scores, loss, gradients and updated parameters remain finite; nonzero cases verify that parameters actually change.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 gives the same six baseline failures and **87 passed, 1 skipped** after the patch.

### History review

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads and 69 pre-existing fork branches, including all 16 reachable item-to-item source versions from 74 commits under current and former paths. The PyTorch variant normalizes in the input dtype; earlier TensorFlow variants use their float32 graph normalization. No previous PyTorch accumulator-promotion correction was found.

- [x] Regressions added to the existing registered item-to-item test module.
- [x] Code comment explains why low-precision accumulation needs promotion.
- [x] Commit includes the required `Signed-off-by` trailer.
- [x] Targets `staging`.

actual_prs.title: Reuse the GeoIMC middle-factor square root within inference
actual_prs.head: 1e0d50e49448c5496d50c2c8bf9cb3654d2a47d1
actual_prs.body:
### Description

GeoIMC computes the same middle-factor matrix square root twice in every inference call, once for row features and once for column features. This repeated decomposition dominates the measured small-query cases.

Compute it once and reuse it for both projections within that call. The scoring formula and transformations stay the same. Subsequent calls still recompute from the current weights, and the direct-embedding list path remains independent of the factor matrices.

Fixes #2468.

### Validation and performance

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43904653540) checks exact head `1e0d50e49448c5496d50c2c8bf9cb3654d2a47d1` with the documented Pymanopt revision:

- Python 3.10: NumPy 1.24.4, SciPy 1.10.1, Numba 0.57.1.
- Python 3.11: NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.13.1, Numba 0.61.2.
- Original GeoIMC tests: **12 passed**. Expanded equivalence suite: **26 passed** on both unchanged staging and the patch, without skips.
- Added checks cover float32/float64, filtered entity rows, all three score transformations, direct embeddings, unchanged input matrices and updated weights between calls.
- The complete inference benchmark uses five warmups and 31 alternating measurements with one BLAS thread. Every paired output is bitwise identical within its environment, and square-root calls decrease from two to one.

Python 3.11 runner results for fixed synthetic feature matrices:

| Scenario | Rank | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 943 users × 1,682 items, 128 features | 8 | 2.697 ms | 2.572 ms | 1.05× |
| 1 user × 256 items, 128 features | 32 | 0.686 ms | 0.388 ms | 1.77× |
| 1 user × 256 items, 256 features | 128 | 14.220 ms | 7.366 ms | 1.93× |

The other dependency environment gives 1.04×, 1.77× and 1.91× for the same shapes. These measurements are fixture-specific: large low-rank batches spend most of their time outside the square-root decomposition.

Black and `git diff --check` pass. Benchmark code, all individual timing samples, dependency versions and test logs are included in the validation branch and run artifacts.

### History review

actual_prs.title: Follow SLi-Rec parameter placement after native device moves
actual_prs.head: 4d1b220158d15d93636e565f2298560fe0cb484c
actual_prs.body:
### Description

SLi-Rec stores the device selected at construction in a plain attribute. Native module migration moves parameters but leaves that attribute unchanged, so dataset tensors, regularization and checkpoint loading can use a different device from the model.

Read the device from the item-embedding weights instead. Initial automatic CPU/CUDA selection is preserved; native `to()`, `cpu()` and `to_empty()` then require no separate metadata update. Parameter names and checkpoint tensors remain unchanged.

Fixes #2470.

- Patched full model suite: **17 passed, 2 CUDA-only skips** in both environments.
- Native meta transitions reproduce the original full-forward mixed-device failure and verify batch placement, shapes, dtypes and regularization. Meta cases assess placement rather than numerical predictions.
- A native CPU → meta → CPU round trip restores an actual checkpoint, reproduces every saved prediction exactly and runs finite-gradient SGD steps that change parameters. No mocked device operators are used.
- CUDA-to-CPU tests cover both `cpu()` and `to("cpu")`, including checkpoint loading, prediction and training. They are committed but skipped on these CPU runners; no CUDA execution is claimed.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 gives the same results.

The validation also combines this change with the exact updated attention fix in #2453. Its CPU test no longer assigns device metadata. Combined results are **31 passed, 2 CUDA-only skips** on PyTorch 2.5.1 and **27 passed, 6 skips** on 2.0.1 (two CUDA cases plus four independently confirmed unsupported CPU-half cases).

actual_prs.title: Reject FFM fields before they alias another instance
actual_prs.head: bb40866a7747ffbf2c95021b22ab6b4f488d20d1
actual_prs.body:
### Description

FFM field positions are flattened across the whole batch before bounds are checked. An out-of-range field can therefore land in another training instance: with `field_count=4`, a field numbered 5 on the first row becomes field 1 on the second row. The same input is rejected with batch size 1 but silently changes another example with batch size 2.

Validate each zero-based field index against `field_count` before adding the instance offset. Keep the existing global consistency check and preserve valid sparse fields, repeated fields, empty feature rows, values and ordering.

Fixes #2472.

### Validation

[Independent before/after validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43910433462) checks exact head `bb40866a7747ffbf2c95021b22ab6b4f488d20d1` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- New cases against unchanged staging: **8 failed, 5 passing controls**.
- Patched full FFM and xDeepFM suites: **40 passed** in both environments, with no skipped tests.
- Six loader cases expose forward and backward aliasing across three records.
- Two native xDeepFM training cases reject the malformed input before any optimizer update; model parameters remain unchanged.
- Five valid-data controls compare complete predictions and gradients across single-record and three-record batches for the linear, FM, CIN, DNN and combined paths. They include empty rows, repeated and unsorted fields, signed feature values and the largest valid field.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 also passes all 40 tests.

### History review

Reviewed 1,497 pre-existing upstream PR heads and 69 fork branches. The current FFM dataset and its former TensorFlow iterator/cache implementations contain 24 distinct reachable source versions across 168 commits; none checks the field against its own instance before flattening. Existing batch-size handling does not address this cross-record aliasing.

actual_prs.title: Exclude masked NewsRec positions from the attention shift
actual_prs.head: b890261b4c6df7b10e7e9af511b96e247fe8bf5e
actual_prs.body:
### Description

NewsRec additive attention chooses its stabilizing maximum before excluding masked positions. A high-scoring padding position can drive every valid exponential below the fixed denominator epsilon. Valid title content then disappears, with zero input gradients in float32 and severely attenuated outputs even in float64.

Exclude masked scores before choosing the shift. Keep a finite sentinel so entirely masked rows still return finite zeros with zero gradients. The unmasked path and learned parameter structure remain unchanged.

Fixes #2474.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43913345232) checks exact candidate `b890261b4c6df7b10e7e9af511b96e247fe8bf5e` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- Unchanged NewsRec model suite: **38 passed** in both environments.
- New cases against unchanged staging: **8 failed, 4 passing controls**.
- Patched complete NewsRec model suite: **50 passed** in both environments; no skips.
- Float32 and float64 attention outputs, input gradients and parameter gradients match a reference that physically removes masked positions.
- All-valid masks preserve the unmasked result exactly. Fully masked rows retain finite zero outputs and gradients.
- Both LSTUR user-combination modes run two actual forward/backward/SGD steps. Predictions, losses, every parameter gradient and updated weights match otherwise identical models with title padding removed at the public input. No neural operator is mocked; a width-one convolution keeps the valid word features identical.

actual_prs.title: Keep GeoIMC entity feature projections sparse during training
actual_prs.head: 72b22acedfe747e65e8978f5a67583ef7413fc40
actual_prs.body:
### Description

GeoIMC's dataset normalizer already accepts CSR entity features, and inference can project them with the learned factors. Training still uses dense-on-sparse NumPy products: sparse column features reach the Numba residual kernel as object arrays, while sparse row features produce an object-valued gradient and fail in the actual optimizer.

Keep feature matrices on the sparse-compatible left side of the cost and gradient products. Reassociate the column gradient so it projects the residual into the rank space before multiplying by the column features. This avoids the row-count by column-feature-count intermediate and supports either or both feature matrices being CSR.

The objective, regularization, symmetric middle-factor gradient, solver settings and inference API are preserved. Document the accepted dense/CSR feature combinations in `DataPtr`.

Fixes #2476.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43915173429) checks exact head `72b22acedfe747e65e8978f5a67583ef7413fc40` with the documented Pymanopt revision `fb36a272cdeecb21992cfd9271eb82baafeb316d`:

| Environment | Unchanged original suite | New cases on baseline | Patched full suite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python 3.10, NumPy 1.24.4, SciPy 1.10.1, Numba 0.57.1 | 12 passed | 6 failed, 2 passed | 20 passed |
| Python 3.11, NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.13.1, Numba 0.61.2 | 12 passed | 6 failed, 2 passed | 20 passed |

No tests are skipped. Local Python 3.12.14 gives the same results.

- All four dense/CSR feature combinations are compared with an independent full-matrix objective evaluated at observed entries.
- Central finite differences check every entry of all three factor gradients, using symmetric perturbations for the middle factor.
- Actual Pymanopt/Numba optimization starts from identical factors, decreases the objective, and matches the dense reference's learned factors.
- Held-out row entities then produce matching cold-start inference scores. Caller feature values and their sparse representations remain unchanged.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass.

No solver, sparse operation or numerical kernel is mocked. The reduced intermediate follows from the multiplication order; this PR does not claim a measured peak-memory or runtime improvement.

### History review

Reviewed 1,497 pre-existing upstream PR heads, 69 fork branches and all 11 reachable optimizer source versions across 60 commits, including earlier paths and intermediate commits. Both historical optimizer formulations retain the dense-on-sparse products. The shared inference square-root change in #2469 is independent and does not alter training.
